variants.headline: A company goes under
variants.sub: The colony has seen the failure of {company}.
variants.body:
The company {company} has gone under. The failure is a business event, not a detailed account of its consequences for particular people. Readers considering {target} should distinguish that known outcome from unreported claims about creditors, employment or the circumstances that brought the company to this position.

The gazette records the company failure without describing an unreported distribution of assets or liabilities. The failure itself and subsequent legal or administrative arrangements require separate accounts. Precision is necessary where a commercial event could otherwise be enlarged into assumptions about individuals, public obligations or the course of proceedings.

We take a sympathetic view of {target}. A failed enterprise does not establish every accusation of poor conduct, and fair assessment must survive an outcome that makes easy blame particularly tempting. Care in the public record is part of responsible administration.
